breakingChangesNotes:
- The `compromised/breached` collection is now `compromised/breacheddb`, and the *collection_name* argument of ***gibti-local-search*** accepts only the new name. An instance that selects `compromised/breached` in *Collections to fetch* stops fetching with *Collection compromised/breached is obsolete; use compromised/breacheddb instead* until you update the selection.
- The `compromised/breacheddb` collection is fetched through a `seqUpdate` cursor, so its first fetch after you select it starts from *Incidents first fetch*; an early date fetches a large backlog. A credential that appears in several leaks makes one incident per record ID, leak name and upload time, and a breached record that carries a password or another credential is a High incident.
- The `compromised/mule` collection is removed from both integrations, and ***gibti-get-compromised-mule-info*** and ***gibtia-get-compromised-mule-info*** are deprecated: they fail with an error naming ***gibti-get-compromised-spd-info***. A feed instance that selects `compromised/mule` in *Indicator collections*, or a ***gibti-local-search*** call with it, stops with *Collection compromised/mule is obsolete; use compromised/spd instead*.
- Feed instances that select `compromised/bank_card_group` or `compromised/masked_card` stop with a message until you remove them. Neither collection yields indicators anymore: the lookup commands and the incidents' extraction leave out the `cnc` block of their records.
- Threat report incidents no longer fill **GIB Is Tailored**, and threat report lookups return no *isTailored*. To count the reports fetched through your hunting rules, use **GIB Fetched With Hunting Rules**, as the **GIB TI Tailored Threats** widget does.
- No Group-IB incident type runs the **Incident Postprocessing - Group-IB Threat Intelligence & Attribution** playbook automatically anymore. Of the types the integration still creates, **GIB Compromised Account Group**, **GIB Compromised Masked Card**, **GIB Data Breach**, **GIB OSI Git Leak** and **GIB OSI Public Leak** ran it on every new incident. Start the playbook from the incident, or turn on *Run playbook automatically* in the incident type.
- Incidents of `suspicious_ip/open_proxy` are named `Suspicious IP Open Proxy: <address>:<port>`, one per port the proxy is listed on. Update rules, playbooks and searches that match the bare address in the incident name.
- The pack's mapper names **GIB Data Breach** incidents after the leak (`leakName`) instead of `Data Breach: <ID>`. Update rules, playbooks and searches that match the old name.
- Phishing group incidents are named after the phishing domain, followed by the impersonated brand in parentheses when the record names one other than the domain, instead of the brand alone. Update rules, playbooks and searches that match the brand in the incident name.
- The **GIBIncidentUpdate**, **GIBIncidentUpdateAllTypes** and **GIBIncidentUpdateIncludingClosed** scripts are deprecated in favor of **GIBTIIncidentUpdate**, **GIBTIIncidentUpdateAllTypes** and **GIBTIIncidentUpdateIncludingClosed**. The pack's pre-processing rules run the new scripts, and rules you created keep working on the deprecated ones. The deprecated scripts copy only the incoming incident's name, occurred time, details and custom fields onto every matching incident; they no longer copy its type, severity, owner or status. **GIBIncidentUpdate** and **GIBIncidentUpdateIncludingClosed** overwrite the occurred time, which they left unchanged before.
- The new scripts update an existing incident only when it has the incoming incident's type, the same **GIB Proxy Port** for an open proxy, and the same **GIB Leak Name** and **GIB Upload Time** for a **GIB Data Breach** incident. An incident whose type an analyst changed by hand no longer receives the updates of its record: the record opens a new incident. Records of different types that share an ID, such as an IP that two `suspicious_ip/*` collections list, no longer merge into one incident.
- The lookup commands write one War Room entry per indicator type, with a context entry and DBotScore per indicator, instead of one entry per indicator field holding all its values, and their indicators report the DBotScore vendor `GroupIBTI` instead of `GIB TI`.
- The feed and the lookup commands no longer create indicators from victim or hosting infrastructure other than the defaced URL and, in the feed, a DDoS target when *Collection filters* names **GIB Victim IP**, as in `attacks/ddos: kinds = URL, Domain, IP, GIB Victim IP`. Existing indicators of these kinds are not removed but will not be refreshed. The feed's `compromised/account_group` indicators no longer include the service URL, and their C&C IPs, in the feed and the lookup commands, no longer carry the compromised user's ASN and location.
  - The defaced site's domain and IP in `attacks/deface` and the domain and hosting IP in `attacks/phishing_group` stay on the incidents only.
  - The `osi/git_repository` collection yields no indicators in the incidents integration and only the repository URL in the feed, with no file revision hashes or committer e-mail addresses.
- Threat report files are keyed by their SHA-256, else SHA-1, else MD5, else SHA-512, instead of their MD5 in both integrations. An existing indicator keyed by the MD5 of a file that also has a stronger hash is not removed but will not be refreshed.
- Incidents extract indicators from the observables of their record only. **GIB Related Indicators Data** no longer carries attributes such as ASNs, countries, registrars, file names or the links of a CVE description, and phishing group and defacement incidents extract URLs only. The field holds one observable per line instead of the JSON of the record's indicators block, so a script that parses it as JSON needs to read lines. The e-mail addresses of phishing kits move to **GIB Related Emails**, which also lists those of the email-message entries of threat reports.
- Nessus, Red Hat, Microsoft and other `osi/vulnerability` advisories whose id is not a CVE id no longer become CVE indicators.
- Lookup and feed indicators take the verdict of their record's collection, or their own Group-IB score where the record has one (`ioc/primary`, payment details). Lookup indicators were *Unknown*, and feed indicators took the instance's *Indicator Reputation*, whose default changes from `Suspicious` to empty. An instance created before 4.0.0 keeps the value it was saved with, `Suspicious` by default; clear *Indicator Reputation* to use the collection verdicts.
- ***ip*** reads Group-IB risk scores on Group-IB's own scale: 0-39 *Good*, 40-79 *Suspicious* and 80-100 *Bad*. 3.0.4 read 0-49 *Good*, 50-84 *Suspicious* and 85-100 *Bad*, so an IP that scores 40-49 is *Suspicious* instead of *Good*, and one that scores 80-84 *Bad* instead of *Suspicious*. ***domain***, which ignored risk scores, maps Group-IB's domain score the same way. *GIBTI.Scoring.score* of ***gibti-ip-scoring*** gives the band of the same scale.
- With a risk score below 40, ***ip*** and ***domain*** return *Suspicious* when `ioc/primary` lists the IP or domain, and ***ip*** also when a `suspicious_ip/*` collection lists the IP (by default every one, at any age; see *Collections that keep an IP at least Suspicious* and *Suspicious IP listing recency (days)*), so a Tor exit or a proxy that 3.0.4 rated *Good* by its risk score reads *Suspicious*. Without a risk score, the result is *Unknown* unless such a listing exists. ***ip*** and ***domain*** read no `ioc/common`, and `hi/open_threats` posts and defacements do not decide: ***domain***, which 3.0.4 rated *Bad* or *Suspicious* from `ioc/common` and *Suspicious* from `hi/open_threats` posts and defacements, can read *Good* or *Unknown* where it read *Bad* or *Suspicious*.
- ***file*** also reads `ioc/primary`: a hash it lists with a risk score of 80 or more is *Bad*, and a hash only it lists, with a lower risk score or none, is *Suspicious*, where 3.0.4 returned *Unknown*. A hash `ioc/common` lists stays *Bad*, and an `ioc/common` record counts only when its hashes include the hash.
- The new *Lookup timeout (seconds)* setting, default 20, limits how long one value of ***ip***, ***domain*** and ***file*** waits for its Group-IB requests. A request that has not answered by then is left out. When a request that decides the verdict is left out or fails with an error other than HTTP 403 or 404, a verdict is set only if no missing answer could have raised it; without one, the indicator keeps the verdict it has. Before, they waited for every request.
- ***gibti-ip-scoring*** sends no request for a value that is not an IPv4 address and returns no indicator or score for it.
- The *id* argument of ***gibti-get-suspicious-ip-vpn-info***, ***gibti-get-suspicious-ip-scanner-info*** and ***gibti-get-malware-malware-info***, and the *ip*, *domain* and *file* arguments of ***ip***, ***domain*** and ***file***, are required.
- Incident severities change: **GIB Malware CNC** incidents are High, **GIB Malware** incidents take the profile's threat level instead of Unknown, and **GIB OSI Git Leak** incidents take the worst grade of the repository and its files. Review severity-based rules, SLAs and widgets.
- Phishing groups that Group-IB marks as false positives or allow-lists no longer become incidents, and the feed no longer creates their indicators. Where **GIB Rule All Types** runs, turn on *Pass flagged phishing groups to the pre-processing rule* to have the rule set **GIB False Positive** or **GIB Allow Listed** on the group's open incident; a flagged group still opens no incident.
- The `gibti-get-<collection>-info` lookup commands relate their indicators to **Malware** and **Threat Actor** indicators unless *Create relationships* is cleared, and the platform auto-extracts their indicator tables, except a defacement's.
- Feed indicators take the TLP of their record, such as RED or AMBER, when the instance sets no *Traffic Light Protocol Color*.
- The context of the lookup commands changes under `GIBTI.<Collection>.indicators`: keys are renamed or removed, such as `events_ipv4_ip` (now `event_ipv4`), `asn`, `country_name` and `region` on compromised accounts, `target_domain` and `target_ip_*` on defacements, `phishing_domain_domain`, `phishing_domain_registrar`, `ipv4_ip` and `ipv4_country_name` on phishing groups, `cnc` on C&C records and `dateLastSeen` (now `dateModified`) on vulnerabilities; the card collections and `osi/git_repository` carry no indicators block. *GIBTI.SuspiciousIPOpenProxy* is keyed by its new `listing` field (`<address>:<port>`).
- ***gibti-get-threat-info*** and ***gibti-get-threat-actor-info*** write their records under *GIBTI.GIBCybercriminalThreatReport*, *GIBTI.Nation-StateCybercriminalsThreatReport*, *GIBTI.GIBCybercriminalThreatActorProfile* or *GIBTI.Nation-StateCybercriminalsThreatActorProfile*, by the collection each record comes from, instead of the *GIBTI* root. Update playbooks and scripts that read these records from *GIBTI*.
- Field formats change: **GIB Threat Actor Name** and **GIB Threat Actor ID** on **GIB Malware** incidents are comma-separated text, **GIB ID** of **GIB Data Breach** incidents is text, and **GIB Nation-State Cybercriminals Threat Countries** is comma-separated text.
- **GIB Phishing Kit Source** is no longer filled on phishing group incidents; read **GIB Phishing Sources**.
- ***gibti-local-search*** applies *date_from* and *date_to*, which it ignored, fails when *date_to* is set without *date_from*, and returns each record's own `seqUpdate` instead of the page's.
- ***ip***, ***domain***, ***file*** and ***gibti-ip-scoring*** return an error entry for a value whose lookup gets no answer, instead of no data, and fail the whole command when the key is refused (HTTP 401, and HTTP 403 for ***gibti-ip-scoring***), so a playbook task without *Continue on error* stops. ***ip*** writes an IPv6 address under *IPv6*.
- Incident times follow the event and are in UTC: a DDoS incident is dated by the start of the attack, and Tor node and open proxy incidents by their last sighting.
- With *Skip updated incidents (prevent duplicates)* on, the integration remembers a record by its collection and ID, an open proxy by its address and port, and a breached record by its ID, leak name and upload time: an IP that several `suspicious_ip/*` collections list opens one incident per collection, where earlier versions opened one.
- Feed instances create a Bad **Malware** or **Threat Actor** indicator for each malware family and threat actor named by a record that yields indicators, apart from a defacer's handle, and relate those indicators to them, unless *Create relationships* is cleared.
- CVE indicators of the feed and ***gibti-get-osi-vulnerability-info*** take their CVSS score and vector from Group-IB's score across CVSS versions (`mergedCvss`) when the record has one, instead of `cvss.score`, so the score of a CVE can change.
- ***gibti-global-search*** lists every collection the API reports, including those ***gibti-local-search*** and the lookup commands do not read; filter on *GIBTI.search.global.supportedByPack* before passing *apiPath* on.
- ***gibti-ip-scoring*** no longer writes *DBotScore* or *IP.Address* and sets no verdict on the indicator, so it never lowers the verdict of ***ip***. Read the risk score from *GIBTI.Scoring.riskScore* and its verdict band from *GIBTI.Scoring.score*.
- ***ip*** no longer writes *IP.Geo.Country*, *IP.Geo.Description* or *IP.Description* from WHOIS: the country is where the range is registered and the descriptions were network remarks. *IP.ASOwner* holds the owner of the autonomous system only when the registry names it, and *IP.Organization.Name* the organization that holds the range instead of the network name; the full record is in ***gibti-ip-whois***. This version does not clear the values earlier versions wrote to existing indicators.

See the 4.0.0 release notes for the full list of changes.
